We need to find a retrosynthetic template that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the described reaction: cycloaddition where two unsaturated parts combine, forming a ring, forming a C-C bond, breaking a C-O bond, losing ketone and C-C triple bonds functional groups. The forward reaction: formation of C-C bond, breaking C-O, losing ketone and alkyne. So retrosynthetic step: break a C-C bond (the new sigma bond) and form a C-O bond (i.e., reverse). Also functional groups lost: ketone and alkyne are present in product? Actually product loses them, meaning they were present in reactants? Wait: In forward reaction, you start with unsaturated molecules (maybe alkyne and carbonyl) and they combine to form cyclic product, losing ketone and alkyne groups. So product (our target) is cyclic product lacking ketone and alkyne. So retrosynthesis: we need to break a C-C bond to generate precursors that contain a ketone and an alkyne (or carbonyl and alkyne). Also break C-O bond? Actually forward reaction breaks C-O, so retrosynthesis forms C-O bond (i.e., we need to add a C-O bond to precursors). So we need a template that breaks a C-C bond and forms a C-O bond, and functional groups formed in forward: maybe a ketone and alkyne are broken (i.e., they are present in reactants). So in retrosynthesis, we need to generate precursors that have a ketone and an alkyne.

We have target SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O

Let's detect functional groups. Use detect_functional_groups.
